import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from io import StringIO
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Prepare the dataset
csv_data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 7), dpi=100)

# Create the scatter plot
# Use 'hue' for transaction type and 'size' for amount to encode multiple variables
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='hour_of_day',
    y='amount',
    hue='transaction_type',
    size='amount',
    sizes=(100, 1000),  # Range of bubble sizes
    alpha=0.8,
    style='transaction_type', # Use different markers for each type
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customize the plot for clarity and insight ---

# Set title and labels with more descriptive text
ax.set_title('Transaction Analysis: Amount vs. Hour of Day', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=12)

# Format the y-axis to display as currency
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.2f')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Set axis limits to give some padding
ax.set_xlim(0, 24)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['amount'].max() * 1.15) # 15% padding on top

# Customize the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the legends for type (hue/style) and amount (size)
type_legend_indices = [i for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label in df['transaction_type'].unique()]
size_legend_indices = [i for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label not in df['transaction_type'].unique() and label != 'transaction_type' and label != 'amount']

type_handles = [handles[i] for i in type_legend_indices]
type_labels = [labels[i] for i in type_legend_indices]
size_handles = [handles[i] for i in size_legend_indices]
size_labels = [labels[i] for i in size_legend_indices]

# Place the legends outside the plot area for better readability
legend1 = ax.legend(type_handles, type_labels, title='Transaction Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)
ax.add_artist(legend1) # Add the first legend back to the plot
if size_handles: # Only add size legend if it exists
    legend2 = ax.legend(size_handles, size_labels, title='Amount', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add grid for better readability
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Ensure everything fits without overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust layout to make space for legends

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

plt.close(fig)
